model.name: Fine-tuned MiniLM evidence NLI
model.architecture: 6-layer RoBERTa-style MiniLM Transformer with three-class pair head

training.checkpoint_selection: Highest pooled validation macro-F1; no test selection
training.base_training_disclosure: The public base checkpoint already learned SNLI and MultiNLI. This project fine-tunes it; it does not pretrain or distil MiniLM from scratch.

data_manifest.task: Evidence-conditioned three-way natural language inference, not article-style or reporting-quality classification

FEVER-NLI.license: Original Wikipedia article terms; fallback CC BY-SA 3.0 per FEVER license
FEVER-NLI.note: Author's Dropbox URL returned HTML rather than ZIP. Mirror claim IDs, claim text and labels verified against every corresponding original FEVER row.

data_manifest.split_strategy: Global normalized claim hashes group all evidence variants. Reserve original FEVER dev, ANLI test, SciFact dev and unused ANLI dev claims before any training sampling. From remaining original training only, select independent seeded label-balanced claim groups for validation/test and cap FEVER/ANLI training (one pair per claim). SciFact retains all remaining claim-document pairs, with 25 groups per primary label reserved for each internal holdout. External sets retain source labels/distributions except documented empty-input, regression-topic, exact-pair duplicate/conflict and cross-source claim-overlap exclusions; no balancing is applied to external data.
data_manifest.cleaning: Unicode NFC, HTML entity decoding, whitespace only. Preserve negation, numbers, case and punctuation; no stemming or stopword removal. No source metadata, label explanations or ANLI model labels enter inputs.
data_manifest.nasa_regression_policy: Exclude every pair mentioning Ingenuity from all prepared sets; provided NASA article is never added to training or calibration.

fever_orientation.canonical_claim_text: Original FEVER claim text after whitespace/HTML normalization

scifact.pairing: One pair per claim/cited abstract (union with annotated evidence documents); full title and abstract, not oracle-selected rationale sentences.
scifact.neutral_semantics: Cited abstracts without annotated evidence: annotators did not find support/contradiction in that abstract, as documented in official doc/data.md.

limitations: Exact normalized claim grouping does not guarantee all paraphrases, event families or shared evidence documents are isolated.

FEVER external uses retrieved evidence with original claim verdicts; retrieval failures can produce a claim/evidence mismatch. Empty evidence is excluded and counted, so these are not official full benchmark scores.
Internal label-balanced splits are a controlled diagnostic distribution, not natural internet prevalence.
Original SciFact dev is a reported external benchmark, not used for fitting; evidence abstracts can be shared across official source partitions.
NLI predicts consistency with supplied evidence; it cannot establish that the evidence source is accurate or current.
Public benchmark text may have appeared in upstream language-model pretraining. Our own fine-tuning/checkpoint/calibration partitions are isolated as documented.

evaluation_protocol.note: Every pair is scored alone, matching the deployed inference path.

calibration.warning: These are validation-fitted pair-relation scores, not calibrated probabilities that the real-world claim is true.

export_verification.note: Measured floating-checkpoint versus quantized-export consistency, not a factual accuracy estimate.

baseline.name: TF-IDF pair features + multinomial logistic regression
baseline.features: TF-IDF(premise), TF-IDF(hypothesis), absolute difference, elementwise product
baseline.context_note: The lexical baseline sees both full texts; the neural model uses a joint truncated token window.

limitations: Pair classification does not independently verify source reliability or establish a universal fact verdict.
Neutral means the supplied evidence is insufficient, not that the claim is false.
A retrieved passage can support only part of a compound claim; whole-claim coverage needs separate review.
Pair benchmarks do not measure URL extraction or evidence retrieval quality.
The base model was already trained on SNLI and MultiNLI; those are not independent new downstream tests.
Calibration and validation precision targets can fail under domain, source or temporal shift.
Long evidence/claim pairs are truncated jointly with longest-first tokenization.
